chapter: Gillespie and Carter on John Collins
title: Gillespie: Collins versus Charlie Christian
summary: Gillespie says Christian was a blockbuster but not as deep as Collins, whose rhythm playing changes chords constantly, and he would rather play with him than anyone.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: When -- Leonard __________, he said that John was one of the Charley Christian inspired guitarists but then you said that John was the prime influence --
-- in New York up until the time --

Yeah. You see, let me show you the difference in the plane. Christian wasn't as deep as John. You see, Christian was a blockbuster, you know. That area that he came from produced that -- guys that played like that, one note. He'd take one note and run you crazy, you know, Charley Christian, and Charley Christian recognized the talents of John Collins.

He recognized it. He knew he was bad, you know, and we used to talk about him. We used to talk about John Collins with Charley Christian. "What do you think of John Collins". He'd say, "Whew", because I'm telling you --

No, he was in another -- another -- I imagine -- I imagine he did, you know, because John was a master progressionist -- you know progressionist -- going from here to here to here to here to here to here. Christian was a

-- let's see, how would you call that -- well he -- Christian was the first one that was heard because he was the first one to play electric guitar. The rest of the guys -- John used to play -- he'd be playing and rhythm, you should hear him play rhythm. Every chord -- you see, every stroke he makes is a different change. He don't say, "bang, bang, bang, bang", he says, "dom ding dum dum ding dum", you know what I mean?

He'll play, you know, he don't make one chord. You know, like you're in a bar, if you've got one chord in a bar now he's progressing all the time. It's a joy to play with a guy like that, really. I don't know nobody that I'd rather play with than him.
I really don't. He's a bad cat. I recognize his talent -- a long time. Shoot, we're out here ain't we?
Shoot, we've got 35 minutes. Find the musicians and let them know that I'm going to make it.
